title: Config Optimizer: Suggest & Safe-Apply for Batching/Caching with Multi-probe Quality Sentinels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Config Optimizer service that generates ranked batching and KV-cache configuration proposals, validates them automatically against a multi-probe quality sentinel suite, and provides a safe-apply workflow with progressive rollout and automated rollback throttles. The optimizer should produce human-readable diffs, risk scores, and a suggested canary-sampling plan. We want a system that can safely reduce per-token cost by opportunistically increasing batch sizes and cache TTLs while ensuring semantic/regression risk remains below route-specific acceptance thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Config optimizer produces candidate set with delta in expected cost and percentile latency per route
Every candidate is validated by the sentinel suite with pass/fail and per-metric deltas reported
Automatic safe-apply executes a 3-stage rollout (shadow -> canary (1-5%) -> ramp) with automated rollback if metrics cross thresholds
Human review link and one-click abort available during canary phase
All changes logged with before/after kernels, quantization hints, and telemetry hooks for tracing regressions
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Suggestion engine - sample recent traffic to create per-route candidate configs and compute estimated cost/latency impact
Phase 2: Sentinel harness - implement multi-probe evals (embedding similarity, structured-field match, token-level perplexity delta, and task-specific checks) and baseline storage
Phase 3: Safe-apply orchestrator - shadow apply + collect outputs, run sentinel comparisons, and automate canary rollout with abort policies
Phase 4: Integrations - console UI for reviewing proposals, API endpoints for programmatic apply, and telemetry to cost/latency dashboards
Phase 5: Hardening - statistical tests, false-positive tuning, and runbook for manual rollback scenarios
test_plan: Unit tests for suggestion heuristics and cost estimation model
Synthetic traffic runs to validate batching/caching behavior across sequence length distributions
Sentinel acceptance tests using a curated anchor set plus stratified random samples per customer route
A/B canary runs comparing baseline to candidate with automated gating logic in a staging cluster
Chaos tests: simulate node failures and scaled-down capacity during rollouts to ensure graceful fallback
rollout_plan: Start in staging with a small traffic slice (shadow mode) for 48h
If sentinel pass, promote to canary at 1% for 4h, then 5% for 8h with stricter thresholds on high-importance routes
If canary is green, ramp to 25% for 24h while monitoring cost and quality signals, then to 100% over 72h
Automated rollback if any per-route metric breaches pre-defined deltas or if p-value from regression test < 0.01
Manual approval gate required before 25% ramp for any route with customer_impact == high
monitoring: Per-route eval metrics exposed in Console (embedding cosine change, structured field F1, token overlap)
Cost and latency delta panels with per-model and per-hardware breakdown
Automated alerts for rate of false positives in the sentinel suite and alert on sudden increases in rollback frequency
Post-rollout canary audit that stores golden pair artifacts for later forensic analysis
notes: We intentionally avoid a single metric; combination of semantic similarity + task-specific checks reduces brittle pass/fail cases.
Must support pluggable sentinel probes so we can add hallucination detectors or domain-specific validators later.
Proposed default acceptance thresholds are conservative; ops can opt-in to aggressive tuning via a per-tenant policy.
Consider an allowlist of routes (low-risk) for faster ramp and a denylist for regulated routes requiring manual review.
